notes.text: With weeping — Some think that it had been better translated, they went weeping; for though the verb be the future tense in the Hebrew, yet that tense has often the signification of the preterperfect tense, thus it answereth, Psalm 1xxvi, 5, 6. He that goeth forth weeping, bearing precious seed, shalt doubtless come again rejoicing. There is a weeping for joy, as well as for sorrow, and thus the text corresponds with that, Zech xii, 10. I will pour upon them the spirit of grace and supplications, and they shall look upon him whom they have pierced, and mourn. By rivers - And they shall have no want as they had when they came out of Egypt, through the wilderness, where they often wanted water.

Hath redeemed — God will as certainly do it, as if he had already done it. In their deliverance as well from Babylon as Egypt, they were types of the deliverance of God's people, by Christ; as well as in their entering into Canaan, they were types of the saints, entering into heaven.

And sing — All the phrases in this verse signify one thing, the happy state of the Jews, after their return from captivity. The height of Zion means the temple. A watered garden - They shall be a beautiful, flourishing, and growing people. Soul seems here to be taken for the whole man. Not sorrow - In that manner they have been. But under these expressions is also promised the spiritual joy which the true Israel of God will have under the gospel, and the eternal joy they shall have in heaven.

glossa.text: *The remnants of Israel.* Which are saved according to the election.

*Behold, I will bring them,* etc. Through the apostles and apostolic men who are the watchmen, crying on the mountain of Samaria, to whom it is commanded: *Sound ye forth, sing ye ((III Reg. XVIII))*, etc.

*The lame man. ((ID.))* To such it is said through Elias: *How long halt ye upon both feet?* But afterwards they ran in Christ; and, *he that walked in darkness hath seen a great light.*

*They shall come with weeping, and in,* etc. ((ID.)) The Jews think this to have been fulfilled, etc., *as far as* they can prove that these things were fulfilled.
*And Ephraim.* Ephraim, who is a type of the Gentile people, etc., *as far as* he first obtained the kingdom in Samaria, etc.

*Out of the hand of one mightier,* etc. ((ID.)) Of the adverse power, which is by nature the stronger: but we are the stronger by faith, if indeed we are set free by him who binds the strong man, and plunders his house.

*The soul of the priests.* Who have the knowledge of God, of whose mouth they ask the law, who believe in him who is a priest for ever.

*With fatness, and my people shall be filled with my good things, saith the Lord,* etc. Whence the Lord was seized in the valley of Gethsemani, that is, of fatness.

notes.text: Thy gates — Thy strength consists not in thy walls, and gates, and bars, but in his protection.
Borders — In all thy land, even to its utmost borders.
Commandment — Which is sufficient without any instruments to execute whatsoever pleaseth him. Swiftly - The thing is done without delay.
Like wool — Not only in colour and shape, and softness, but also in use, keeping the fruits of the earth warm. Ashes - In colour and smallness of parts, as also in its burning quality.

Ice — Great hail-stones, which are of an icy nature, and are cast forth out of the clouds, like morsels or fragments. An exhortation to all creatures in heaven and earth, man especially, to praise God, ver. 1-14.

glossa.text:
*Alleluia.* This psalm works the love of the Jerusalem to come. It is said to be of Aggeus and Zacharias, who in the captivity prophesied the restoring of Jerusalem, which, as Jeremias foretold, was accomplished after seventy years, that is, after the rolling round of the whole of time, which is carried on in seven days.

*Praise, O Jerusalem.* ((CASS.)) This whole psalm proclaims the power of God. First, it tells the good things of the Jerusalem to come; secondly, it tells what good things are given here to the saints, there: *Who sendeth forth.* ((AUG.)) The prophet, being as yet set in captivity, etc., *as far as* we who have heard him thus pouring it forth.

*He hath strengthened the bolts of thy gates.* ((AUG.)) Note that the door is shut, the prudent virgins being admitted and the foolish shut out, so that now none may go out or come in. And fitly after the admonition to praise he subjoins concerning the shut gates: for with the gate of Jerusalem shut she praises securely, because none has gone out for whom she should grieve; none comes in whom she should fear, whence scandals should be.
*With the fat of corn.* ((ID.)) With the bread that came down from heaven: in the world he is shut up in flesh, known by faith alone; then shall he be seen as he is.

*Who sendeth forth his speech.* The second part subjoins what gifts are given here to the elect, through which the truth of that which is to come may be known.

*To the earth.* ((AUG.)) That he may be known on earth. For unless to send *mittere*; read *mitteret*, "he were to send" his word to the earth, by which we are weighed down and hindered from our returning, we should not be lifted up to the fat of corn that satisfies. For in the earth, where we labour weary, faint, sluggish, cold, that is, in the desert, he forsakes us not, but manna: *who sendeth forth his speech,* etc.

*Swiftly runneth.* ((AUG., CASS.)) Or even unto swiftness, that is, from God, so that it is swiftness itself, than which nothing could be said more choicely or more expressly.

He says not that the word is swift, that it be swift with a swiftness of which it partakes more or less: but than swiftness itself, whereby all other things are called swift, nothing is swifter. And again, that which is swift, as a horse is swift to a man, is not so everywhere: but swiftness itself is everywhere, it is not in a part. To the Word of God it belongs not to be in a part, but to be everywhere through himself. This is that wisdom *which reacheth from end to end mightily,* yet not by motion of place, but by immobility. And of the spirit of wisdom also it is said, *driven, moveable, sure, undefiled;* this swiftness effects, that it be both always everywhere, and nowhere held shut in. But who is sufficient to think upon these things? Yet there is hope of laying hold of the Word, because he has predestinated us.

*Who giveth snow,* etc. ((AUG.)) To the earth. For charity growing cold, etc., *as far as* and while he calls these to penance, *he scattereth mist like ashes.*

((ID.)) *He scattereth mist like ashes,* etc. Ashes pertain to penance, etc., *as far as* and who has predestinated and has called to penance. According to the letter: God scatters snow like wool, mist like ashes, he makes crystal like morsels of white bread. For crystal is a certain kind of thing after the manner of glass, but it is white: and it is said to be snow hardened by ice through many years, so that it cannot be dissolved.

*His crystal,* etc. That is, the obstinate, who are not dissolved easily as snow is.

*He sendeth as morsels,* etc. Otherwise, *as crumbs of bread,* that they may feed others, that they may preach the truth which they assail. All together, one bread; singly, morsels; whence: *Being many, we are one bread in Christ ((I Cor. X))*. Paul was crystal, hard and shining: hard, because he persecuted the Church; shining, because he was skilled in the law. But God dissolved him, and he was made bread, who taught the truth. But unless he dissolve,

*Before the face of him, of God, who shall stand?* Otherwise, shall subsist. ((AUG.)) It is cold when he forsakes, calls not, pours not in grace: and who else shall dissolve it? None. Whence the Apostle: *Who shall deliver me from the body of this death? ((Rom. VII.))* As if he said: I grow cold, none dissolves me, unless the grace of God *send forth his word.*

*He shall send out his word, and shall melt it.* ((CASS.)) For when the word of God comes, neither cold, nor darkness, nor hardness can despair. For they are melted healthfully, and pour out streams of spiritual benefit to others whereof they may drink, according to that saying: *All you that thirst, come to the waters ((Isa. LV))*.

notes.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us — God's blessing us is his bestowing all spiritual and heavenly blessings upon us. Our blessing God is the paying him our solemn and grateful acknowledgments, both on account of his own essential blessedness, and of the blessings which he bestows upon us. He is the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, as man and Mediator: he is his Father, primarily, with respect to his divine nature, as his only begotten Son; and, secondarily, with respect to his human nature, as that is personally united to the divine. With all spiritual blessings in heavenly things - With all manner of spiritual blessings, which are heavenly in their nature, original, and tendency, and shall be completed in heaven: far different from the external privileges of the Jews, and the earthly blessings they expected from the Messiah.
As he hath chosen us — Both Jews and gentiles, whom he foreknew as believing in Christ, 1 Pet. i, 2.

Having predestinated us to the adoption of sons — Having foreordained that all who afterwards believed should enjoy the dignity of being sons of God, and joint-heirs with Christ. According to the good pleasure of his will - According to his free, fixed, unalterable purpose to confer this blessing on all those who should believe in Christ, and those only.
To the praise of the glory of his grace — His glorious, free love without any desert on our part.

By whom we — Who believe. Have - From the moment we believe. Redemption - From the guilt and power of sin. Through his blood - Through what he hath done and suffered for us. According to the riches of his grace - According to the abundant overflowings of his free mercy and favour.
In all wisdom — Manifested by God in the whole scheme of our salvation. And prudence - Which be hath wrought in us, that we may know and do all his acceptable and perfect will.

Having made known to us — By his word and by his Spirit. The mystery of his will - The gracious scheme of salvation by faith, which depends on his own sovereign will alone. This was but darkly discovered under the law; is now totally hid from unbelievers; and has heights and depths which surpass all the knowledge even of true believers.

That in the dispensation of the fulness of the times — In this last administration of God's fullest grace, which took place when the time appointed was fully come. He might gather together into one in Christ - Might recapitulate, re-unite, and place in order again under Christ, their common Head. All things which are in heaven, and on earth - All angels and men, whether living or dead, in the Lord.

Through whom we — Jews. Also have obtained an inheritance - The glorious inheritance of the heavenly Canaan, to which, when believers, we were predestinated according to the purpose of him that worketh all things after the counsel of his own will - The unalterable decree, "He that believeth shall be delivered;" which will is not an arbitrary will, but flowing from the rectitude of his nature, else, what security would there be that it would be his will to keep his word even with the elect?

That we — Jews. Who first believed - Before the gentiles. So did some of them in every place. Here is another branch of the true gospel predestination: he that believes is not only elected to salvation, (if he endures to the end,) but is fore-appointed of God to walk in holiness, to the praise of his glory.

In whom ye — Gentiles. Likewise believed, after ye had heard the gospel - Which God made the means of your salvation; in whom after ye had believed - Probably some time after their first believing. Ye were sealed by that Holy Spirit of promise - Holy both in his nature and in his operations, and promised to all the children of God. The sealing seems to imply,

1. A full impression of the image of God on their souls.

2. A full assurance of receiving all the promises, whether relating to time or eternity.

Who, thus sealing us, is an earnest — Both a pledge and a foretaste of our inheritance. Till the redemption of the purchased possession - Till the church, which he has purchased with his own blood, shall be fully delivered from all sin and sorrow, and advanced to everlasting glory. To the praise of his glory - Of his glorious wisdom, power, and mercy.

glossa.text: *Blessed.* The salutation having been set first, he begins from the giving of thanks, intimating that all things are from God. *He hath blessed.* The word of blessing is indeed one, but according to what befits the person it must be understood in various ways. God is blessed by man, when he is extolled with worthy praises. But man is blessed by God, when God imparts to him the gifts of his grace, not by that man's merits, but by his own mercy.

*Even as he chose,* etc. Let no one, then, suppose that souls are eternal with God, and that they then merited something, according to the error of those who say that before these visible things there were certain holy souls, and that they were therefore then chosen.

*Who predestinated.* A predestination having been set down which pertains to the justice and holiness of the present life, another is here set down pertaining to eternal life, whose effect he noted above.

*Unto the praise of the glory of his grace,* etc. As if he should say: the glory of the graces is the eternal adoption. *In which he hath shown grace.* The effect of the first preordination unto justice. *In the beloved Son.* God the Father loving his only-begotten, the Son lavishes divine things upon those whom he loves and to whom he wills.
*In whom we have,* etc. He shows a twofold grace, because he both redeemed, and did not impute our sins.
*Which hath superabounded.* Thus far concerning those things which [he gave] to the whole human race: now he speaks of those which he gave to the apostles singularly.

*In the dispensation.* That is, in the fullness of the time dispensed by God, that is, in this time of grace, in which the divine providence reasonably dispensed to fulfil the things which in other times were promised or prefigured. For if men were utterly ignorant, not taught beforehand, they would not receive Christ, and unless the proud had first been convicted by the natural and the doctrinal law, they would little esteem the coming of Christ.

 *To restore. ((AUG.))* Now those things are restored which are in the heavens, etc., *as far as* they are renewed from the oldness of corruption.

*All things, which are in the heavens.* That is, the angels; or: *to restore,* that is, to fill up. *Which are in the earth.* That is, men, who had been depraved by sin. *In him.* That is, through Christ.

*In whom we also.* Lest the apostles, in whom grace superabounds, should seem to have deserved better than others, he shows that they were thus called freely, not by merits, even as others also were. *By lot.* Grace is called a lot, because it is not the choice of man, but of the will of God. Whence the Lord's tunic woven from above, which signifies charity, came by lot. *He worketh all things.* Even to will the good, and that we should begin to believe, so that by our example no one may glory in man. For it is true: *You have not chosen me, but I you,* etc. And the praise of the glory of God is when many are gained unto the faith, as the glory of a physician is when he cures many.
*In whom you.* Now he comes to those things which he gave to the Ephesians. *When you had heard. When* here notes the cause, and the time.

In him was life — He was the foundation of life to every living thing, as well as of being to all that is. And the life was the light of men - He who is essential life, and the giver of life to all that liveth, was also the light of men; the fountain of wisdom, holiness, and happiness, to man in his original state.
And the light shineth in darkness — Shines even on fallen man; but the darkness - Dark, sinful man, perceiveth it not.
There was a man — The evangelist now proceeds to him who testified of the light, which he had spoken of in the five preceding verses.

The same came for (that is, in order to give) a testimony — The evangelist, with the most strong and tender affection, interweaves his own testimony with that of John, by noble digressions, wherein he explains the office of the Baptist; partly premises and partly subjoins a further explication to his short sentences. What St. Matthew, Mark, and Luke term the Gospel, in respect of the promise going before, St. John usually terms the testimony, intimating the certain knowledge of the relator; to testify of the light - Of Christ.

Who lighteth every man — By what is vulgarly termed natural conscience, pointing out at least the general lines of good and evil. And this light, if man did not hinder, would shine more and more to the perfect day.
He was in the world — Even from the creation.
He came — In the fulness of time, to his own - Country, city, temple: And his own - People, received him not.

But as many as received him — Jews or Gentiles; that believe on his name - That is, on him. The moment they believe, they are sons; and because they are sons, God sendeth forth the Spirit of his Son into their hearts, crying, Abba, Father.

Who were born — Who became the sons of God, not of blood - Not by descent from Abraham, nor by the will of the flesh - By natural generation, nor by the will of man - Adopting them, but of God - By his Spirit.

Flesh sometimes signifies corrupt nature; sometimes the body; sometimes, as here, the whole man. We beheld his glory — We his apostles, particularly Peter, James, and John, Luke ix, 32. Grace and truth - We are all by nature liars and children of wrath, to whom both grace and truth are unknown. But we are made partakers of them, when we are accepted through the Beloved. The whole verse might be paraphrased thus: And in order to raise us to this dignity and happiness, the eternal Word, by a most amazing condescension, was made flesh, united himself to our miserable nature, with all its innocent infirmities. And he did not make us a transient visit, but tabernacled among us on earth, displaying his glory in a more eminent manner, than even of old in the tabernacle of Moses. And we who are now recording these things beheld his glory with so strict an attention, that we can testify, it was in every respect such a glory as became the only begotten of the Father. For it shone forth not only in his transfiguration, and in his continual miracles, but in all his tempers, ministrations, and conduct through the whole series of his life. In all he appeared full of grace and truth: he was himself most benevolent and upright; made those ample discoveries of pardon to sinners, which the Mosaic dispensation could not do: and really exhibited the most substantial blessings, whereas that was but a shadow of good things to come.

John cried — With joy and confidence; This is he of whom I said - John had said this before our Lord's baptism, although he then knew him not in person: he knew him first at his baptism, and afterward cried, This is he of whom I said. &c. He is preferred before me - in his office: for he was before me - in his nature.

And — Here the apostle confirms the Baptist's words: as if he had said, He is indeed preferred before thee: so we have experienced: We all - That believe: have received - All that we enjoy out of his fulness: and in the particular, grace upon grace - One blessing upon another, immeasurable grace and love.

The law — Working wrath and containing shadows: was given - No philosopher, poet, or orator, ever chose his words so accurately as St. John. The law, saith he, was given by Moses: grace was by Jesus Christ. Observe the reason for placing each word thus: The law of Moses was not his own. The grace of Christ was. His grace was opposite to the wrath, his truth to the shadowy ceremonies of the law. Jesus - St. John having once mentioned the incarnation (ver. 14,) no more uses that name, the Word, in all his book.
No man hath seen God — With bodily eyes: yet believers see him with the eye of faith. Who is in the bosom of the Father - The expression denotes the highest unity, and the most intimate knowledge.

glossa.text: *In the beginning was the Word.* Against those who, on account of Christ's temporal nativity, said that Christ had not always been, he begins with the eternity of the Word, saying: *In the beginning was the Word.*

*All things were made by him. ((AUG.))* He is not a creature, through whom every creature was made, etc., *as far as* which all agree unto the power of the Divinity.

*And without him was made nothing. ((ORIG.))* Thus he divides it: *And without him was made nothing.* The order is: *There is nothing which was made without him.*
*What was made, was life in him. ((AUG.))* John Chrysostom: *And without him was made nothing. What was made.* Hilary: *Without him was made nothing, which was made in him.*

*There was a man sent.* After he had ascended by a lofty flight beyond every nature into the height of theology, because he had contemplated that the Word had always been with the Father, he presently descends to the lowliness of human nature, and particularly of the Word's forerunner, against those who said that human nature had been in the first parent wholly lost and brought to nothing. *A man sent.* A man, not an angel, as the heretics will have it, sent from God. Therefore he was able to speak of God.

*He was the true light.* Every man is said to be that nature in man which was made to the image and to the likeness of God. All the other things which are in man are the lower parts of man, and are in a manner outside the man. In that, namely, the soul, as in a certain higher world, the true light shines, and it enlightens those coming into that world and being born again through grace, because they whose life and conversation is in the heavens are as it were in another world.
*And his own received him not.* From the beginning of the world there was no time in which there were not receivers of the divine word; whence he adds: *But as many as received him.*

*To be made the sons of God.* A wondrous power, that they who were sons of the devil should, set free through him, be called both sons of God and brethren of Christ. But by what order they are made sons of God, and how this generation differs from the carnal, is subjoined: *Who not of bloods.*

*And the Word was made flesh.* But that we may securely believe that men are born of God, he subjoins that God is born of man: by this taking on of infirmity our infirmity is healed, that we may be able to be made sons of God. And this is it: *And the Word was made flesh.* That which was above descended below. What wonder: if that which was below ascended into that which is above? Nor is it a wonder if men are born of God, since God was born of man. *Full of grace and truth.* The man Christ was full of grace, because, with no merits going before, from the time he was conceived the Godhead was in him, filling that man with all fullness, redounding into all the saints; whence his mother also is called not only the mother of a man, but also the mother of God. Nor is it a wonder if a man is also called God, since God is also called man. And this is called grace and truth, because it was so promised of old and now exhibited: namely, that God should be in the man, filling him with every good, and through him his own.

*This was he of whom I said.* By the demonstrative pronoun it is intimated that Christ was present in that place. For often the Lord himself, still unknown, before he was baptized and preached, was wont to come to John. *Who is to come after me.* Who is born after me, who is to preach after me, to baptize, to die. Not that he was not already born when he said these things, since he had even been baptized: but he was to come in preaching, in death, but not in resurrection. *He was made before me, because he was prior to me.* From the Greek, he was made in my presence, that is, he appeared to me indeed, namely, because he was prior to me.

*And of the fullness.* The forerunner's testimony having been set forth, the evangelist returns to the testimony of his own assertion. As if he should say: *The Word was made flesh: we saw his glory, full of grace and truth, and of his fullness we all have received.* Grace, that we may believe in him, and truth, by which we shall understand him. *We have received. ((AUG.))* Not only the grace which is plainly given gratis, not for merit, as the faith which works through love, by which the just man lives, but in return for that one, grace, that is, eternal blessedness, which is also called the wage of justice, and grace also, because the merit is from grace. *Grace for grace.* Grace is given in the conceiving of the good through grace. Grace simply, which is not of merit; if afterwards we work with it, we grow accustomed to good things, and then grace is given for the former grace.
*By Moses.* By Moses the servant, the foretelling; by the Lord Jesus, the fulfilling of salvation.

*No man hath seen God at any time.* That is, no mere man living in this body has seen God as he is; whence it was said to Moses: *Man shall not see me and live ((Exod. XXXIII))*, that is, no one living in the body shall see my divinity. Whence God added these things to Moses: *Stand in the hole of the rock, and when I shall have passed through, thou shalt see my back parts ((Ibid.))*. The rock, that is, Christ; the hole, the gibbet of the cross; *I shall have passed through*, that is, I shall pass over from the world to the Father. The back parts: his birth, his passion, his resurrection, his ascension, through which, being believed, we come to his blessedness and to the sight of him. That which is read, that God appeared to men either visibly to the eyes of the flesh, or invisibly in prophetic visions, is to be understood as done through a creature made subject to him; for the visions of the prophets were wrought by a certain spiritual creature, in which they are declared to have seen God.

*The only-begotten Son,* etc. What the sum of grace and truth may be he briefly subjoins, namely, the knowledge of the Trinity itself; whence: *This is life eternal, that they may know thee the one true God, and Jesus Christ whom thou hast sent.* Which in this life is not full, because no one in the flesh has seen God as he is. Whence neither Moses himself, much less was grace given through him, as he himself also, after all the things seen in the figure of God, said: *Show me thyself ((Exod. XXXIII))*, but the Son, who is in the secret of the Father, has declared him, *because no one knows the Father but the Son, and he to whom the Son shall have willed to reveal him ((Luc. X))*. He himself declares to his own what is to be held concerning the Trinity of the Godhead, and how it is to be come to, and he leads them into it.

echoes.text: Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, from everlasting and to everlasting! Amen and amen.
echoes.note: 'Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ' reproduces the Jewish berakah formula 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,' which closes Book I of the Psalter. Volume is high (verbatim opening 'Blessed be the God'); recurrence across the Psalter (41:13; 72:18; 106:48) and Israel's liturgy makes the form availably and thematically coherent as the native idiom of doxological praise.

echoes.text: Praise be to Yahweh God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous deeds.
echoes.note: The eulogetos opening directly imitates the doxological berakah 'Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel,' another Psalter book-closing blessing. Recurrence with 41:13 and 106:48 establishes the form as a standing liturgical pattern Paul Christologically reworks ('the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ'). Thematic coherence with the eulogetos genre is exact.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God. Yahweh your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth. Yahweh didn’t set his love on you, nor choose you, because you were more in number than any people; for you were the fewest of all peoples: but because Yahweh loves you, and because he desires to keep the oath which he swore to your fathers, Yahweh has brought you out with a mighty hand, […]
echoes.note: 'He chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we would be holy' transposes Israel's election: 'the LORD has chosen you to be a people for his own possession... holy.' Volume is strong (the verb 'chose' + the purpose 'holy'); recurrence in Deuteronomy's election theology and thematic coherence (gratuitous love, not merit) make this the controlling OT subtext for predestination language.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God, and Yahweh has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth.
echoes.note: 'The LORD has chosen you to be a people for his own possession... a holy people' supplies both the election verb and the 'holy/possession' pairing that Ephesians 1:4 and 1:14 develop. Recurrence with Deut 7:6 reinforces a settled Deuteronomic formula; thematic coherence with adoption and inheritance is high.

echoes.text: You shall tell Pharaoh, ‘Thus says Yahweh, Israel is my son, my firstborn,
echoes.note: 'Adoption as children' (huiothesia) presupposes Israel's sonship: 'Israel is my son, my firstborn.' Volume is conceptual rather than verbal, but recurrence (Hos 11:1; Jer 31:9) and thematic coherence with election and inheritance make Israel's adoptive sonship the OT matrix Paul universalizes in Christ.

echoes.text: and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” Abram gave him a tenth of all.
echoes.note: Melchizedek's 'Blessed be God Most High' is the patriarchal prototype of the berakah Paul deploys. Availability and thematic coherence (blessing the God who delivers and gives) support the link, though the volume is lower than the Psalter parallels, since the verbal overlap is only the opening 'Blessed be God.'

echoes.text: “Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘You shall be holy; for I, Yahweh your God, am holy.
echoes.note: 'Holy and without defect before him' draws on the Holiness Code's 'You shall be holy, for I... am holy,' and the sacrificial demand that an offering be 'without blemish' (Lev 1:3; 22:21). Thematic coherence (Israel/offering presented blameless to God) is strong; the volume is diffuse because two strands of Levitical holiness merge.

echoes.text: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.
echoes.note: 'When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son' ties adoption to redemptive love and election, the same cluster Ephesians 1:4-6 fuses ('in love... adoption'). Recurrence with Exod 4:22 strengthens the sonship motif; the volume is thematic, marked medium because Ephesians does not cite the wording.

echoes.text: He said, “Now take your son, your only son, whom you love, even Isaac, and go into the land of Moriah. Offer him there for a burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will tell you of.”
echoes.note: 'The Beloved' (en to egapemeno) evokes Isaac, 'your son, your only son, whom you love,' the beloved offered son — apt for a passage moving toward 'redemption through his blood.' Thematic coherence (beloved son, sacrifice) is good; the volume is moderate because 'Beloved' also draws on Psalm 2 and Isaiah 5 traditions.

echoes.text: I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
echoes.note: The royal decree 'You are my son; today I have begotten you,' read messianically in Second-Temple Judaism, undergirds the 'Beloved' Son in whom believers are adopted as sons. Recurrence of Psalm 2 in NT sonship texts and thematic coherence (divine sonship grounding adoption) support a medium-confidence echo.

echoes.text: Let me sing for my well beloved a song of my beloved about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a very fruitful hill.
echoes.note: Isaiah's Song 'for my beloved' (to egapemeno LXX) is one of the LXX loci where ho egapemenos functions almost titularly, a possible reservoir for Ephesians' 'in the Beloved.' Availability is genuine, but volume and thematic coherence are weak here, so the echo is marked low and contested.

echoes.text: Therefore tell the children of Israel, ‘I am Yahweh, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments:
echoes.note: 'Redemption' (apolytrosis) maps onto the exodus paradigm: 'I will redeem you with an outstretched arm.' Volume is conceptual but strong; recurrence of redemption-from-Egypt language across the OT and thematic coherence with deliverance and possession (cf. 1:14) make the exodus the governing pattern for 'redemption through his blood.'

echoes.text: Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, “Look, this is the blood of the covenant, which Yahweh has made with you concerning all these words.”
echoes.note: 'Redemption through his blood' coupled with covenant draws on the blood of the covenant Moses dashed on the people, 'the blood of the covenant the LORD has made.' Thematic coherence (blood ratifying covenant deliverance) is solid; volume is moderate because Ephesians names redemption and forgiveness rather than covenant explicitly.

echoes.text: But now thus says Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
echoes.note: 'I have redeemed you; I have called you by name; you are mine' fuses redemption, calling, and possession exactly as Ephesians 1:7,14 do. Isaiah's new-exodus redemption is availably and thematically coherent with Paul's apolytrosis; medium because the link is motivic, not verbal.

echoes.text: Israel, hope in Yahweh, for with Yahweh there is loving kindness. With him is abundant redemption. He will redeem Israel from all their sins.
echoes.note: 'With the LORD... is plentiful redemption. He will redeem Israel from all his iniquities' joins redemption to forgiveness of sins, the precise pairing of Ephesians 1:7 ('redemption... the forgiveness of our trespasses'). Thematic coherence is high; volume moderate, so medium confidence.

echoes.text: but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head on your bed, are these: as for you, O king, your thoughts came on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what shall happen.
echoes.note: 'Making known to us the mystery of his will' draws on Daniel's God 'who reveals mysteries' and 'made known... what will be.' Volume is strong (mysterion + the verb 'make known' is distinctively Danielic in the LXX); recurrence (Dan 2:19,30,47) and thematic coherence (eschatological disclosure of God's hidden purpose) make this the primary subtext for Ephesians' mystery language.

echoes.text: The king answered to Daniel, and said, Of a truth your God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, since you have been able to reveal this secret.
echoes.note: 'Your God is... a revealer of mysteries, since you could reveal this mystery' reinforces the Danielic provenance of 'the mystery of his will' made known. Recurrence within Daniel 2 strengthens the allusion; medium because it overlaps with 2:28-29 rather than adding distinct wording.

echoes.text: declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things that are not yet done; saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure;
echoes.note: 'Him who works all things after the counsel of his will' echoes Isaiah's God 'declaring the end from the beginning... my counsel shall stand, and I will accomplish all my purpose.' Thematic coherence (sovereign counsel/purpose executed in history) is strong; volume is moderate, hence a medium echo.

echoes.text: All the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing; and he does according to his will in the army of heaven, and among the inhabitants of the earth; and no one can stay his hand, or ask him, What are you doing?
echoes.note: 'Works all things after the counsel of his will' resonates with Daniel's confession that God 'does according to his will... none can stay his hand.' Availability and thematic coherence (universal divine sovereignty) support a faint echo; volume is low, so it is marked contested.

echoes.text: The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat; The calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf together; and a little child will lead them. The cow and the bear will graze. Their young ones will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the ox. The nursing child will play near a cobra’s hole, and the weaned child will put his hand on the viper’s den. They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain; for […]
echoes.note: 'To sum up all things in Christ, the things in the heavens and the things on the earth' may resonate with Isaiah's eschatological reconciliation of all creation under the Messianic shoot. Thematic coherence (cosmic harmony restored under the Anointed) is plausible but the volume is low; marked contested.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
echoes.note: 'Sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise' draws on the eschatological promise 'I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh.' The Spirit as 'of promise' coheres with Joel's prophetic gift inaugurating the last days; recurrence in Second-Temple expectation and thematic coherence (Spirit marking the eschatological people) support a high-confidence allusion.

echoes.text: I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: 'I will put my Spirit within you' is the new-covenant promise behind the indwelling 'Spirit of promise.' Thematic coherence (Spirit given to a redeemed possession, cleansed and made holy) matches Ephesians' election/holiness frame; recurrence with Ezek 37:14 and 39:29 strengthens the link.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God, and Yahweh has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth.
echoes.note: 'The redemption of God's own possession' reproduces Deuteronomy's 'a people for his own possession (peripoiesis/segullah).' Volume is strong on the possession motif; recurrence (Deut 7:6; 26:18; Exod 19:5) and thematic coherence (redeemed people belonging to God) make this a controlling subtext for 1:14.

echoes.text: Now therefore, if you will indeed obey my voice, and keep my covenant, then you shall be my own possession from among all peoples; for all the earth is mine;
echoes.note: 'You shall be my own possession among all peoples' (segullah / LXX laos periousios) underlies 'the redemption of God's own possession.' Recurrence with Deut 7:6 and 14:2 and thematic coherence (covenant possession claimed and redeemed) reinforce the allusion; the volume on the possession concept is high.

echoes.text: In that day, says Yahweh of Armies, will I take you, Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel,’ says Yahweh, ‘and will make you as a signet, for I have chosen you,’ says Yahweh of Armies.”
echoes.note: 'You were sealed' (esphragisthete) evokes Haggai's 'I will make you like a signet ring (sphragis), for I have chosen you,' which joins the seal image to divine election — the very pairing of Ephesians 1:4,13. Thematic coherence is strong; medium because the seal in Ephesians is the Spirit, not the person.

echoes.text: For he said, “Surely, they are my people, children who will not deal falsely:” so he was their Savior. In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bore them, and carried them all the days of old.
echoes.note: 'They are my people... so he became their Savior... he redeemed them' joins God's people, Spirit, and redemption — the cluster of Ephesians 1:13-14. Thematic coherence is decent but the volume is faint, so this is a low, contested echo.

echoes.text: They shall be mine,” says Yahweh of Armies, “my own possession in the day that I make, and I will spare them, as a man spares his own son who serves him.
echoes.note: 'They shall be mine, says the LORD of hosts, my own possession (segullah)' on the day God acts could reinforce 'the redemption of God's own possession' with an eschatological cast. Recurrence of the segullah term supports availability; volume is low, hence contested.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: With all these I sought rest; And in whose inheritance shall I lodge? Then the Creator of all things gave me a commandment; And he that created me made my tabernacle to rest, And said, Let your tabernacle be in Jacob, And your inheritance in Israel. He created me from the beginning before the world; And to the end I will not fail. In the holy tabernacle I ministered before him; And so was I established in Sion. In the beloved city likewise he gave me […]
echoes.note: Wisdom seeks a resting place among the nations and is given Israel as her inheritance; the motif of the agent of creation coming to her own people who variously receive or reject her underlies vv.10-11. Thematic coherence with the Wisdom-rejection pattern is strong; medium for lack of verbal contact.

echoes.text: Because I have called, and you have refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no one has paid attention; but you have ignored all my counsel, and wanted none of my reproof; I also will laugh at your disaster. I will mock when calamity overtakes you; when calamity overtakes you like a storm, when your disaster comes on like a whirlwind; when distress and anguish come on you. Then will they call on me, but I will not answer. They will seek me diligently, […]
echoes.note: Wisdom calls but is not received ('I called and you refused'), the rejection-of-Wisdom topos behind 'his own didn't receive him' (v.11). The motif of the personified divine agent spurned by her people coheres tightly with John's tragic note.

echoes.text: [source text not in the World English Bible]
echoes.note: Wisdom finds no dwelling place among humans and returns to heaven, the most pointed Second-Temple parallel to the Word coming to his own and being rejected (vv.10-11). Pseudepigraphal but genuinely warranted here: the Wisdom-withdrawal pattern matches John's reversal closely. Contested as to direct dependence.

echoes.text: You are the children of Yahweh your God. You shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead.
echoes.note: 'You are the children of the LORD your God' supplies the divine-sonship category recast as the 'right to become God's children' (v.12). Low confidence; the sonship-of-God-people motif is broad across the OT.

echoes.text: Of the Rock who became your father, you are unmindful, and have forgotten God who gave you birth.
echoes.note: 'The God who gave you birth' offers a God-as-begetter image behind 'born... of God' (v.13). Faint and contested, but coheres with the divine-generation language that replaces ordinary descent.

echoes.text: Yet the number of the children of Israel will be as the sand of the sea, which can’t be measured nor numbered; and it will come to pass that, in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’
echoes.note: 'You are children of the living God,' the promise of new divine sonship to those who were not a people, resonates with becoming God's children by birth from God (vv.12-13). Low confidence; thematic rather than verbal.

echoes.text: Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them. According to all that I show you, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all of its furniture, even so you shall make it.
echoes.note: 'The Word became flesh and lived (eskēnōsen, 'tabernacled') among us' deliberately evokes the sanctuary that God commanded so he might 'dwell among them.' The tabernacle-pitching verb is the load-bearing figural cue: the incarnate Word is the new tent of meeting. High volume and thematic coherence.

echoes.text: Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and Yahweh’s glory filled the tabernacle. Moses wasn’t able to enter into the Tent of Meeting, because the cloud stayed on it, and Yahweh’s glory filled the tabernacle.
echoes.note: The glory of the LORD filling the tabernacle is the template for 'we saw his glory' (v.14): the indwelling Word manifests the kabod that once filled the tent. The tabernacle-plus-glory pairing makes the figural reading near-certain. High coherence and recurrence with the Sinai cycle.

echoes.text: Yahweh passed by before him, and proclaimed, “Yahweh! Yahweh, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth,
echoes.note: 'Full of grace and truth' renders the LXX/Hebrew formula 'abounding in steadfast love (hesed) and faithfulness ('emet)' from God's self-revelation to Moses. This is the densest verbal-conceptual borrowing of the Prologue's climax (vv.14,17). Very high thematic coherence: the glory Israel saw at Sinai is now seen in the Word.

echoes.text: He said, “Please show me your glory.” He said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and will proclaim Yahweh’s name before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.” He said, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.” Yahweh also said, “Behold, there is a place by me, and you shall stand on the rock. It will happen, while my glory passes by, that I will put you in a cleft of […]
echoes.note: Moses' request to see God's glory, granted only as a passing of God's goodness while his face remains unseen, undergirds both 'we saw his glory' and 'no one has seen God at any time' (vv.14,18). The contrast (Moses denied the face; the Son makes God known) is structured directly on this scene.

echoes.text: He said, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.”
echoes.note: 'No one has seen God at any time' (v.18) closely restates 'you cannot see my face, for no one may see me and live.' High volume and a near-citation level of verbal coherence; the Son's making-God-known answers the Sinai limitation.

echoes.text: Then the Creator of all things gave me a commandment; And he that created me made my tabernacle to rest, And said, Let your tabernacle be in Jacob, And your inheritance in Israel.
echoes.note: Wisdom is commanded to 'pitch her tent (kataskēnōson) in Jacob,' the closest Second-Temple antecedent to the Word tabernacling among us (v.14). The tent-pitching verb plus the creation-agent identity makes Sirach 24 a primary source for the whole Prologue. High coherence and recurrence.

echoes.text: He gave to Moses, when he finished speaking with him on Mount Sinai, the two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets, written with God’s finger.
echoes.note: 'The law was given through Moses' (v.17) refers to the Sinai giving of the tablets 'written with the finger of God.' The Moses-law / Christ-grace antithesis is built on the Sinai law-giving as its foil. Secure availability and strong thematic coherence.

echoes.text: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mountain, Moses didn’t know that the skin of his face shone by reason of his speaking with him. When Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come near him. Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the rulers of the congregation returned to him; and Moses spoke to them. […]
echoes.note: Moses' face shining with reflected glory after seeing God contrasts with the Son who is himself the glory and declares the Father (vv.14,18). The Sinai-radiance scene reinforces the Moses-versus-Word comparison; medium for absence of direct verbal borrowing here.

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to you out of the midst of the fire: you heard the voice of words, but you saw no form; you only heard a voice.
echoes.note: At Horeb Israel heard a voice but 'saw no form,' the unseen-God theme behind v.18. The motif of God unseen yet now declared by the Son coheres with John's Sinai contrast; medium confidence.

echoes.text: then I was the craftsman by his side. I was a delight day by day, always rejoicing before him,
echoes.note: Wisdom beside God as the delighting child/craftsman supports 'the one and only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father' (v.18), the intimate, eternal closeness of the agent to God. Coheres with the Wisdom substrate established in the opening; medium.

echoes.text: For she is a breath of the power of God, And a clear effluence of the glory of the Almighty; Therefore can nothing defiled find entrance into her. For she is an effulgence from everlasting light, And an unspotted mirror of the working of God, And an image of his goodness.
echoes.note: Wisdom as the radiance of God's glory and image of his goodness underlies 'we saw his glory' and the Son as the one who makes the unseen God known (vv.14,18). Reinforces the glory/visibility theme; medium for conceptual rather than verbal link.

echoes.text: ‘Yahweh is slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, forgiving iniquity and disobedience; and that will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, on the third and on the fourth generation.’
echoes.note: The 'grace and truth' (hesed-we-emet) divine-attribute formula recurs in Moses' intercession, strengthening recurrence of the Exodus 34:6 source behind v.14/17. Listed low because Exodus 34:6 is the primary locus; this is a secondary witness.

echoes.text: Mercy and truth meet together. Righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
echoes.note: 'Steadfast love and faithfulness meet together' pairs hesed and 'emet, the same word-pair behind 'grace and truth.' Faint and contested as a direct source, but evidences the recurrence of the formula in Israel's vocabulary.

harmony.title: The Word made flesh
harmony.note: John alone begins before time itself — "In the beginning was the Word" — where the others begin with a birth or a baptism.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Sing for joy; the Lord has gathered his people home.
The Word became flesh, full of grace and truth.
They shall be radiant over the goodness of the Lord.
The Word became flesh, full of grace and truth.
From his fullness we have received grace upon grace.
Come, let us worship. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Imagine a long road home — the scattered being gathered, the weeping turned to dancing.
The Word became flesh and lived among us.
God has gathered us from far places and turned our mourning into joy.
The Word became flesh and lived among us.
For the Word who was in the beginning has come and made his home with us.
The Word became flesh and lived among us.
And from his endless fullness we receive grace, and then more grace.
The Word became flesh, full of grace and truth!

lines: The scattered gathered, mourning turned to dancing.
The Word became flesh and lived among us.
The Word of the beginning makes his home with us.
The Word became flesh and lived among us.
